statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is elevated as Nasdaq-100 futures weaken into a high-stress rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: orange. The main danger window covers renewed premarket weakness through ADP, the cash open, Factory Orders and EIA data; later de-escalation depends on observed retracement quality.
headline: Renewed premarket weakness lifts Tail above the block threshold
body: Nasdaq-100 futures were about 0.6% lower in later premarket reporting after roughly 0.2% earlier. The 10-year yield was above 4.8%, Brent near $95, and fresh supplementary context showed broad semiconductor and megacap weakness. The alignment lifts Tail above 25%, but repeated failed retracements are not yet independently verified.

lookbackSummary: Tail rose from the low 30s into the high 40s on September 1, then fell into the low 20s overnight as mean reversion returned. Brief re-elevations at 05:00 and 07:00 UTC faded by 09:00, while Stress stayed extreme.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours center on ADP, the U.S. open, the Beige Book and Broadcom. Forecast Tail is elevated only where persistent extension or failed retracements could emerge; scheduled events themselves mainly raise Stress.

forecast.analysis: Later premarket reporting had Nasdaq-100 futures down about 0.6%, versus roughly 0.2% earlier. Yields above 4.8%, Brent near $95 and weak semis lift Tail, but repeated failed retracements are not yet verified.

forecast.analysis: Before ADP, elevated Tail persists only if futures stay near lows while yields and oil remain firm. A sustained technology-led rebound would weaken the trend case.
ADP is due at 12:15 UTC. Stress is extreme; Tail stays elevated only if the observed response extends directionally with shallow pullbacks rather than two-way price discovery.
The 13:30 UTC cash open is the next structure test. Tail remains elevated if opening flow extends the move and early retracements fail; deeper pullbacks would reduce it.
Factory Orders at 14:00 UTC and EIA data at 14:30 UTC form a second catalyst cluster. Tail depends on post-data persistence and oil/yield/technology alignment.
After the data cluster, Tail can ease if price discovery turns two-sided. Persistent extension or renewed session-extreme holding would preserve elevation.
Mid-session Tail remains above baseline while rates, oil and geopolitics stay sensitive. Orderly retracement and less-aligned tech pressure would support de-escalation.
With the initial catalysts behind the market, Tail is lower unless directional efficiency persists. Broader rotation and deeper pullbacks would favor mixed conditions.
The Beige Book is due at 18:00 UTC. Tail is elevated only if the release is followed by persistent repricing with poor mean reversion; the event itself mainly raises Stress.
After the Beige Book, Tail moderates if yields and equities stabilize. Sustained cross-asset reinforcement would keep the directional risk elevated.
Late-afternoon Tail falls to watch if deeper pullbacks develop. Oil and long yields can keep Stress high even without a pathological one-way price path.
Broadcom's call is due at 21:00 UTC. Tail rises conditionally only if verified company news produces broad semiconductor/megacap extension with shallow retracements.
Post-call Tail stays elevated only if verified Broadcom information produces broad follow-through. A contained single-stock response would favor faster normalization.
Late-session Tail returns to watch under a two-sided tape. Oil and yield pressure may keep Stress high even if Nasdaq mean reversion improves.
After the U.S. close, gap and headline risk remain, but Tail is lower absent fresh one-way futures evidence. Cross-asset instability remains mainly a Stress driver.
Early Asia retains high background Stress. Tail stays at watch unless fresh futures evidence shows directional extension with limited retracement.
Overnight Tail remains below the block threshold absent verified renewed extension. A geopolitical discontinuity or aligned futures/rates move is the main escalation route.
During the Asia handoff, mixed conditions remain the base case. Tail rises only if fresh futures evidence shows repeated extension or failed retracements.
Approaching Europe, high yields and oil preserve Stress without automatically lifting Tail. Stable futures with meaningful retracements keep watch status.
The European pre-open is a cross-market checkpoint. Tail stays at watch unless futures, yields and oil align into a persistent directional move.
At the European cash open, Tail remains near the watch ceiling. Escalation requires observed one-way futures structure, not the opening event itself.
Through the European morning, macro pressure remains a Stress driver. Tail stays below the block threshold unless shallow pullbacks and repeated extension appear.
drivers: Macro Stress without automatic Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: Later European trading has no U.S. Tier-1 release in this hour. Tail eases if futures remain two-sided; geopolitical or rates acceleration is the main conditional risk.
In the final forecast hour, Tail remains watch-level absent verified one-way structure. Attention shifts toward later U.S. data, which is not treated as already observed.
